# /crav1-plan-from-spec

lane: plan | group: Plan | starter: no | stage: stable | since: 1.0.0 | prompts: 3
purpose: Turn an accepted spec into a file-level plan.md and independently testable tasks.md.
use_when: Spec is accepted
prompt_note: The gate may ask one architecture batch. Leftovers that might be current work or later work are one short batch, current or later, not one question at a time. The closing yes is the third. Skip a batch that does not apply. A value the user left out is outside the budget.
reads: Reads the accepted spec, diagrams, ADRs, exports, kept security findings already written, and `claims.md` when it exists, and, when the spec is partial or `## In the code` names paths, that same committed repo and branch before any task is written.
writes: Writes `plan.md` and `tasks.md`, and matching OpenSpec export files when those already exist. A built piece that already matches v0 is marked already there and gets no rebuild task. A piece the user leaves gets one line in the plan and no task. Lists each kept-open question under Risks without asking whether to park it, and stale research findings under Risks. That does not block the plan. Writes `Blocks: T#`, `Blocks: none`, or `Blocks: whole slice` under a kept-open question. A `Blocks: T#` risk says kept open; blocks those tasks until resolved. A `Blocks: none` risk says kept open; does not block the current tasks. A `Blocks: whole slice` risk says kept open; blocks the whole slice until resolved. A `Blocks:` line wins over that Risk wording. Only a question with no `Blocks:` line keeps do not implement until resolved. Writes an `## Approval needed` item when a constraint says a named person gives a yes before something, with `Person:` and `Holds:`. It does not write `Approved:`.
leaves alone: Leaves `spec.md` alone except a `Blocks:` line under a kept-open question and an `## Approval needed` item from a constraint. Leaves a claimed `In progress:` task line in `tasks.md` unchanged. Leaves application code and any linter install alone.
limits: when `## Linter` says this repo has no linter for the code the tasks will touch, it stops before Build until the user chooses. A line under `## Dismissed test suggestions` is not a task. A kept test suggestion that is already an acceptance line maps to a task. A gap or a disagreement is finish, add a verify test, or leave before any task exists. A later run does not turn a left piece into work unless the user says so. Stale research does not fail the gate.
flow:
- the recap ends with Run next, `Review the plan, which is written and not reviewed yet:` above `/crav1-review-plan <slug>`, no `Next:` line.
- A `## Linter` section that names a tool, or records going on without one, counts as named even beside a partial `No linter ...
- for <part>` line.
- the After writing recap (paths written, task count, acceptance lines no task matched by wording, to compare by meaning first, the dependency waves, verify notes with no kind, kept-open questions and their `Blocks:` lines, approval items, stale research, the linter line and the one `Next` line) is printed by `scripts/plan_check.py recap --vendor copilot`; the agent passes only what it alone knows (built pieces, the branch read, unmapped security checks).
- `plan_check.py order --vendor copilot` checks the waves after `tasks.md` is written.
- The After writing list moved word for word to `references/recap.md`, the plan.md section list and host setup tasks to `references/write.md`.
- a constraint that a named person gives a yes before something becomes an `## Approval needed` item, with `Person:` and `Holds:` for the tasks that do that work.
- It does not write `Approved:`.
- File-level `plan.md` and `tasks.md`; each verify note names the checks before code; names a linter or checker when the repo has one, and stops before Build when it does not; refuses to code and does not install a linter.
- When the spec is partial or `## In the code` names paths, reads that repo and branch and chooses finish the gap, add a verify test, or leave it before any task.
- A piece that already matches v0 is not a choice.
- Built pieces reads every work branch of the spec without checkout (and `../<repo>` for another repo), labels pieces `only on <branch>, not merged`, and ends a task with `(branch: …)` when its piece lives on one branch.
- a task may name a sub-branch of the spec branch, `(branch: feat/orders-capacity-t3)`.
- each kept-open question that does not block the demo becomes its own entry under `## Risks`, without asking whether to park or answer it.
- once `tasks.md` exists, a leftover that blocks some current tasks gets `Blocks: T#` and the risk line says do not implement until resolved.
- A leftover that blocks no current task gets `Blocks: none`, and that risk line does not say do not implement until resolved.
- No `Blocks:` line still means the whole slice.
- a question with `Blocks: T2, T4` gets the risk line `kept open; blocks T2, T4 until resolved.` Only a question with no `Blocks:` line keeps do not implement until resolved.
- A risk matches on the question first sentence or a `(question: <first words>)` tag, not the whole line.
- optional `(step: 1)` links a task to a numbered Approach step, and optional `(map: feat/cancel-refund)` puts that task on another branch.
- a task listed in `claims.md` as `In progress:` is left unchanged: no renumber, reorder, rewrite, or removal.
- After writing `tasks.md`, the step preserves those lines and says once which claimed tasks were kept.
- `plan_check.py order --vendor copilot` also lists branches that wait for each other as a `Branch loop:` line with the recommended fix in plain words.
- Before the recap, apply it on the user's yes with `walk_progress.py fix-loop --root <spec-folder> --pick <n> --yes --vendor copilot`.
- a task that waits for another pull request ends its line with `(after: PR 87)`.
- When the text says `after PR 87 merges` and the mark is missing, `plan_check.py order --vendor copilot` names the line.
- On yes, `plan_check.py after-pr --root <spec-folder> --yes --vendor copilot` writes the mark.
